keyNotes: Written on the sheets: the overall strings (35'-10" front, 28'-8" and 54'-2" west, 25'-6" ell), the strings of window and door widths on the front, the west side and the ell's east side (sliding doors 5'-10" and 5'-11"), the attic gable's windows, and the bay's faces (4'-4", 7'-1 1/8", 4'-4 5/8"). Everything else was measured off the 1-bit TIFFs at 100 pixels a foot (checked against the 35'-10" and 54'-2" strings to within 0.5%). The plans give room numbers, not room sizes.

There is no section. Heights are estimates from the elevations: the window heads are 7'-9 1/4" and 8'-7 1/2" apart (written), so the second floor is taken 8.63 over the first; the ridge is 31'-5" over grade and about 30.5 over the first floor; the ceilings (7.9) are floor to floor less an assumed 0.75 ft of framing. The basement's depth is not drawn: 7.0 is a guess. A judge should hold P3's heights loosely for this house.

Room outlines are the clear floor between the inner faces of the drawn walls (about +-0.2 ft). The 2 ft deep zone between the front and back rooms on each side holds chimney masses and closets; on the first floor its west part (x 0.6 to 10.1) and the small closets beside the east chimney are not rooms of this key. The back parlor takes in the alcove x 10.1 to 14, y 13.6 to 15.2.
The kitchen opens to the dining room and to pantry 106 where the plan draws the old walls dash-dot (open, a beam above); those are openings, not doors.

The ell is one storey: attic 206 over it is unfinished and taken as level with the second floor (the plan draws it there). The way into it, through a small closet by the bath, is not clear on the plan: those doors are marked uncertain.
The deck is outside, a porch of the ell; its two flights of steps go down to the ground. The cellar's bulkhead ('infilled door opening', 'UP' at the ell's north end) is not a way in now.

The research note gives 12 principal rooms; this key has 9 rooms and the hall on the first floor, 5 rooms and the hall on the second, plus closets, landings, the deck, the two attics and the two cellars.
